vqa_framing.title: VQA evaluation instances

criterion_vqa.description: Multi-class value prediction per criterion vs expert annotation

management_vqa.description: Management action prediction vs clinical pathway

agent_vqa.description: Multi-turn clinical interaction: counterfactual, guideline, refusal, and override queries with deterministic ground truth

vqa_framing.framing_note: No standard dermoscopy VQA benchmark exists. Our criterion evaluation against 7-point checklist expert annotations serves the same role as DermAgent's concept annotation on Derm7pt, but (a) evaluates on 4x more cases, (b) predicts multi-class values rather than binary presence, and (c) is validated against the published Argenziano rule (1011/1011 match).

disclosed_differences: MedGuard v2 trains a linear probe on frozen DermLIP features (supervised); DermAgent uses zero-shot cosine similarity. HAM labels are publicly available and training takes minutes on CPU.
Our Derm7pt criterion task is harder (multi-class value prediction) than DermAgent's (binary feature detection). Direct F1 comparison favors them.
Our Derm7pt test classifier metrics had disclosed exposure during design (PREREGISTRATION_V2.json, test_split_exposure). The system's own test performance is genuinely out-of-sample.
what_we_cannot_claim: That the stacked ensemble beats the classifier (P1 failed, p=0.5935)
Superiority over specialized dermoscopy classifiers on raw accuracy
unique_strengths: Criterion ground truth evaluation against expert annotations
Quantified cross-centre transfer boundary (3 negatives as contribution)
Statistical significance tests with multiple comparison correction
